## Project team

::: {.person}
![](people/ryan.jpg){fig-alt="Portrait of Ryan O'Loughlin" width="112" height="112"}

::: {.person-text}
### [Ryan O'Loughlin](https://ryanoloughlin.org/)

[Principal investigator · Assistant Professor of Philosophy]{.role}

<p class="org"><img src="logos/qc.png" alt="" class="logo" width="20" height="20"> Queens College, City University of New York</p>

A philosopher of science who studies how climate scientists gain trustworthy
knowledge from imperfect models. He has worked with scientists at NSF NCAR and
NASA GISS since 2019, and leads the project's philosophical analysis.

<span class="email-obfuscate" data-user="ryan.oloughlin" data-domain="qc.cuny.edu">ryan.oloughlin [at] qc.cuny.edu</span>
· [ryanoloughlin.org](https://ryanoloughlin.org/)
:::
:::

::: {.person}
![](people/matthew.jpg){fig-alt="Portrait of Matthew Mayernik" width="112" height="112"}

::: {.person-text}
### [Matthew Mayernik](https://library.ucar.edu/directory/matt-mayernik)

[Co-principal investigator · Project Scientist and Research Data Services
Specialist]{.role}

<p class="org"><img src="logos/ncar.png" alt="" class="logo" width="20" height="20"> NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research</p>

Studies how scientists create, describe and share data, including how climate
model intercomparisons earn credibility. He co-leads the interviews and
document analysis, and leads the workshop.

<span class="email-obfuscate" data-user="mayernik" data-domain="ucar.edu">mayernik [at] ucar.edu</span>
:::
:::
